bib.title: Is Progressive Disclosure All You Need for Long-Context Agents?

legacy_report:
COVERAGE: 16 of 16 pages read, 64,338 chars, all of it (main text, limitations, references, Appendices A-C). Extraction was clean.

SOURCE: "Is Progressive Disclosure All You Need for Long-Context Agents?" Yifeng He (UC Davis), Yinzhe Zhao (Zhejiang Univ.; work done while interning at UC Davis), Jicheng Wang (UC Davis), Hao Chen (Univ. of Hong Kong). arXiv:2607.17598v1 [cs.AI], 20 Jul 2026. Preprint; the PDF names no venue.

MAIN CLAIM: Progressive disclosure "buys context, not intelligence". On one book it is redundant when the harness already navigates well. Once the corpus grows to many books, a one-level skill pack (flat) is decisive. A second routing level (hierarchical) never helps and sometimes breaks accuracy.

SETUP: The authors turn ∞Bench into an agent environment called LOONGDOC, built on BenchFlow, using the Agent Client Protocol (ACP). They test 3 harnesses (Codex, Pi, Claude-Code) with 3 models (gpt-5.4-mini, qwen3.6-27b, claude-haiku-4.5). The subsets are En.MC, En.QA and Zh.QA. Scoring is deterministic. Approaches compared:
- raw: the book sits in the file system with no skill pack.
- flat: one SKILL.md with a chunk index in its body, plus references/ chunk files.
- hierarchical: each chunk is its own skill with an always-loaded description, plus a meta-router.
- hybrid-rag: BM25 plus BGE-M3, RRF fusion and a BGE reranker. It was run only on Pi.
Packs follow the book-to-skill recipe (Virgilio Jr., 2026). Chunks are cut at chapter headings, with a fallback of about 4000 words.

HEADLINE NUMBERS
1. Single book, Table 1. Each cell is the mean of 3 seeds. The paper does not state the number of questions.
   - Pi gpt-5.4-mini, En.MC: flat 0.9126 vs hierarchical 0.6398 (raw 0.8851, hybrid-rag 0.7628).
   - Pi qwen3.6-27b, Zh.QA: flat 0.7479 vs hierarchical 0.3890.
   - Codex gpt-5.4-mini: raw, flat and hierarchical tie within error on all three subsets. Trajectories show the bare agent greps for the entities in the question.
   - Claude-Code haiku-4.5, En.MC: flat 0.8667 vs raw 0.7448±0.1166.
2. Library scale, Table 2: Codex gpt-5.4-mini, En.QA, K=20 books. raw 0.257±0.067 vs flat 0.462±0.061 vs hierarchical 0.267±0.069. The ± is the standard error across bundles and seeds. Zh.QA raw falls to 0.043 at K=20. flat beats raw on En.QA in all six cells across two harnesses and two models. (Pi's own En.QA at K=20 is only 0.128 raw vs 0.184 flat, and its K=10 cell favours raw.)
3. Cost, Appendix C.2, Codex En.QA at K=20: raw uses 68.3M tokens per question (uncached upper bound, $52). flat uses 32.5M ($25) at nearly double the accuracy. The cost is an uncached upper bound; caching would favour disclosure further.
4. flat beats hybrid-rag on Pi in nearly every cell. For example, on qwen3.6-27b hybrid-rag scores En.QA 0.5439 and Zh.QA 0.5856, against raw 0.6813 and 0.7563.

QUOTES
- p.1 (abstract): "Progressive disclosure buys context, not intelligence: it is redundant while a strong agent can locate the right passages itself, and decisive once the corpus grows too large to navigate by reading."
- p.6: "It reconstructs on the fly the locate-then-read capability that the skill pack pre-builds, so disclosure is redundant when the agent already navigates well natively"
- p.7: "hierarchical always loads every chunk's description, so a twenty-book library inflates the always-on budget and recreates the context pressure that disclosure is meant to relieve"

LIMITS (authors' own, unless marked)
- En.MC books are canonical novels the models probably memorized. This blunts any disclosure signal there.
- Corpus size was sampled only at K∈{1,5,10,20}, in one benchmark family of narrative books. The paper cannot say whether the effect transfers to code or technical manuals.
- Gains are task- and language-specific: they are sharpest on English open QA, and absent or negative on Chinese.
- Chunking and the description recipe were held fixed. Sample sizes are those ∞Bench provides, so many gaps sit within one standard error.
- Appendix C.1: on Pi at library scale, the depth result reverses on open QA. flat falls below raw on Zh.QA, and hierarchical is best at K=20 (0.330). So depth is not uniformly harmful.
- My observations: the K=20 En.MC gap is only "borderline". hybrid-rag was run only on Pi. Models are small or mid-size (haiku-4.5, gpt-5.4-mini, qwen3.6-27b). Nothing was tested on frontier models.

BUILDS ON
- Anthropic 2025, Agent Skills and progressive disclosure (open standard, Dec 2025), and Anthropic 2025, "Effective context engineering".
- Virgilio Jr. 2026, book-to-skill.
- ∞Bench (Zhang et al., ACL 2024).
- Cherny and Wu 2025, Claude Code dropping its RAG index (anecdotal).
- Li et al. 2026, SkillsBench; Zhang et al. 2026, 138K SKILL.md audit; Sun et al. 2026, Corpus2Skill (non-archival).
- Liu et al. 2024 (TACL), lost in the middle; Hsieh et al. 2024 (COLM), RULER.
- Li et al. 2024 (EMNLP Industry), RAG vs long context; RAPTOR (Sarthi et al., ICLR 2024); GraphRAG (Edge et al. 2024).

TARGET-NOTE FIT: 04-retrieval.md fits better. The evidence is on just-in-time loading and on agentic search versus a retriever. It also supports a skills point for 09-protocols.md: keep one routing level, because always-loaded descriptions cost context.
